business_quality.justification: Operating margin 35.9%, free cash flow $857M on $2.74B revenue, and cash conversion of 1.18x operating cash flow to net income - profits arrive as real cash. Operating income rose $0.588B to $0.982B in the latest year and operating cash flow rose alongside it ($750M to $868M), so the jump is organic rather than an accounting artefact. Best-measured company in the screen at 16 of 16 scoring components. Deducted because the underlying growth rate is only about 9% - this is a steady compounder, not a grower.

competitive_advantage.justification: Among the strongest moats in this set. CAD and PLM software holds a manufacturer's entire engineering record - part geometry, revisions, bills of material, supplier data. Migrating means re-validating decades of product data, so switching costs are genuinely punitive and renewal rates are high. The deduction is for competition from Dassault, Siemens and Autodesk, all well-resourced, which caps pricing power even though it rarely causes churn.

catalysts.justification: Real and dated but modest. Q3 FY2026 constant-currency ARR of $2.448B grew 9.1% excluding divestitures, beating the guided 8-9% range, and management RAISED the low end of full-year guidance to roughly 9-9.5%. Operating and free cash flow both came in above the high end of guidance, and $626M of buybacks were executed. Scored only 5 because none of this re-rates a stock: a company growing ARR 9% and guiding to 9% is delivering precisely what is already expected.

risk_reward.justification: Base case +18% against a bear of -25%. The reverse DCF implies the price assumes 8.6% free-cash-flow growth against 32.0% delivered, so the bar is low and clearable. But the upside is correspondingly capped - a 9%-growth business does not re-rate dramatically. This is a moderate and fairly reliable return rather than a 20%-plus candidate.

management.justification: Divested Kepware and ThingWorx in March 2026 to concentrate on the core CAD/PLM franchise, a genuine focus decision rather than empire-building, and returned $626M through buybacks. Beat and raised guidance. Withheld one point because those divestitures make fiscal 2026 GAAP figures noisy and harder for a shareholder to interpret without adjustment.
